reading.title: Words That Do More Than Say
reading.purpose: Meet the special kinds of words and phrases that make language colorful.
paras: Language has many tools that make speaking and writing more colorful. One simple tool is onomatopoeia, a word that sounds like the noise it names. When you read splash, sizzle, or buzz, you can almost hear the sound.

Another tool is the figure of speech, a phrase that means something different from its plain words. If a friend says, "It's raining cats and dogs," no animals fall from the sky. The expression just describes very heavy rain.

A proverb is a short, well-known saying that gives advice, such as "Actions speak louder than words." A pun plays on a word with two meanings. For example, "I used to be a banker, but I lost interest" is a pun because interest can mean money earned or a feeling of curiosity.

Some words depend on who is talking. Slang is casual language that friends share, and it changes quickly. A word that was popular years ago may sound odd today. A dialect is a form of a language spoken in one place or by one group. In one region people ask for a soda, and in another they ask for a pop.

Finally, some pictures symbolize ideas. A dove can symbolize peace, and a heart can stand for love. People associate these pictures with strong feelings because they have seen them used that way many times. Be careful with a cliche, a phrase so common that it has lost its freshness, such as "quiet as a mouse." Try inventing a new comparison instead.

choices: casual words that friends share and that change quickly
a short, well-known saying that gives advice to listeners
a joke that plays on one word with two different meanings
a form of a language spoken in one place or by one group

qs.q: Which sentence explains why a joke about a banker losing interest is a pun?
choices: A proverb is a short, well-known saying that gives advice, such as "Actions speak louder than words."
For example, "I used to be a banker, but I lost interest" is a pun because interest can mean money earned or a feeling of curiosity.
Some words depend on who is talking.
If a friend says, "It's raining cats and dogs," no animals fall from the sky.
qs.why: This sentence shows the two meanings of the word interest, which is what makes the joke a pun.

qs.q: Why do people associate a dove with peace?
choices: Doves are the quietest birds, so people link them with a quiet time.
A dove was the first bird named in a famous old proverb about peace.
They have seen doves used as a sign of peace again and again.
Doves are the easiest birds for artists to draw on a flag.
qs.why: The text says people connect these pictures with strong feelings because they have seen them used that way many times.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only slang and dialect belong in any good piece of writing today.
Doves and hearts are the only pictures that can ever stand for ideas.
A writer should always repeat the same famous sayings to be clear.
Special words and phrases help people say ideas in colorful ways.
qs.why: Every paragraph introduces another kind of colorful language, from onomatopoeia to symbols.
